senses.definition: A people scattered far from a homeland they still keep ties to.
senses.caution: The weight is the whole risk. Stretched to any dispersed group — ex-colleagues of a firm, alumni of a team, people who left a project — it sounds glib to anyone whose family actually belongs to one, and that person is more often in the room than not. If you mean a network of former employees, say alumni network.
senses.example: The growth story there is remittances — money moving back through the diaspora — not domestic demand.

cues.text: A friend describes a wedding where everyone's parents left the same country decades ago and almost nobody has been back.
You are explaining why one neighbourhood has three bakeries selling the same bread from one small region.
You are reading about a language kept alive abroad long after it faded where it began.
You are explaining to a colleague that a country's economy runs largely on money sent home by people living overseas.

distractors: The property of work that runs for many steps before anyone can tell if it worked.
A funded, staffed team that concentrates a scarce capability in one place.
A rule of thumb that gets a good enough answer quickly.
Using far more words than the point needs.
To make a bad situation worse.
